implementation_notes: The JDK's own facade for calling C is the FFM API: SymbolLookup finds the function, FunctionDescriptor describes its signature, and Linker.downcallHandle returns a MethodHandle the facade class invokes - no hand-written C glue, which is what made JNI brittle. The API is final since JDK 22, the jextract tool generates the binding class from the header mechanically, and MemorySegment/Arena carry the native lifetime. The facade keeps the arena alive for as long as it owns the handle and closes through the same binding.
pitfalls: A MemorySegment is only valid inside its Arena's lifetime: a facade that closes the arena while callers still hold segments fails with an exception or crashes the VM.
Downcall handles and upcall stubs are restricted methods: without --enable-native-access they warn or throw IllegalCallerException.
Struct layouts are platform-dependent - Linker.canonicalLayouts() must be consulted instead of hard-coding sizes when the C API passes structs.
An upcall into Java must not throw: an exception escaping a callback terminates the JVM abruptly.

variants.name: JNI with hand-written C glue
variants.implementation_notes: The pre-FFM form: the facade class declares native methods, System.loadLibrary loads the shared object, and a hand-written C layer translates between Java types and the C API. It still works on every JVM and is the only option below JDK 22, but the glue code is part of the wrapper: every acquired string, array and global reference must be released, and the C side must not call back into Java while an exception is pending.
pitfalls: Every GetStringUTFChars/GetPrimitiveArrayCritical needs its matching Release call, and a wrapper that caches jclass/jobject references without NewGlobalRef crashes or leaks.
Returning a Java object to the C side on a borrowed reference can be collected; ownership must be explicit.
setjmp/longjmp and exceptions do not mix: JNI code must clear or check pending exceptions before calling further JVM functions.
